prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (ideological framing removed)

Economy and public finances
- Eliminate most of the structural deficit within a Parliament; create an independent fiscal watchdog; deliver an emergency Budget; cut identified central government waste; freeze most public sector pay for one year (excluding the lowest paid); review bringing forward the rise in the state pension age; scale back tax credits and child trust funds for higher-income households.
- Cancel planned rises in employer/employee National Insurance for most workers, funded by in‑year efficiencies.
- Publish eight economic benchmarks covering stability, rebalancing toward exports/investment/saving, youth employment, competitiveness, regional private‑sector growth, public service productivity, safer banking, and lower emissions.

Jobs, welfare and skills
- Replace multiple schemes with a single Work Programme, with payment by results; reassess incapacity benefits; require community work for long‑term claimants who refuse reasonable job offers.
- Offer a National Insurance holiday for new firms’ first hires; expand apprenticeships and create an all‑age careers service; set colleges freer from central control; add university places and review research assessment.

Business, tax and regulation
- Cut and simplify corporation tax (main and small‑company rates), set a five‑year tax road map, and create an Office of Tax Simplification.
- Reduce red tape via regulatory budgets and open procurement to SMEs; foster innovation and hi‑tech exports; improve R&D credits.
- Consumer finance: new consumer protection body, free national financial advice funded by a levy, fairer card/store card rules, and protection against forced home sales for small unsecured debts.

Infrastructure and regional growth
- Begin a national high‑speed rail network; improve rail franchising and accountability; oppose additional runways at major London airports; link Heathrow to high‑speed rail; reform air duty; support electrification and urban sustainable transport; consider a fuel duty stabiliser.
- Accelerate nationwide superfast broadband using existing infrastructure access.

Health and social care
- Real‑terms funding rises; expand patient choice across accredited providers; publish comparative outcomes; GP‑led commissioning; cut NHS administration costs; end non‑clinical targets.
- 24/7 urgent care access; single non‑emergency number; protect local maternity/A&E where safe; expand single rooms to fight infections; Cancer Drugs Fund.
- Integrate health and social care budgets for long‑term conditions; support carers and hospices; voluntary insurance option to protect homes from residential care costs; stronger public health with targeted funding.

Families and early years
- Remove the “couple penalty” in tax credits as savings allow; recognise marriage and civil partnerships in tax; two‑year council tax freeze via central savings.
- Extend flexible working rights; introduce flexible parental leave; support diverse childcare; refocus Sure Start on early intervention; add health visitors; bolster relationship support; tighter rules on marketing to children.

Education
- Raise teaching standards and discipline; support phonics and early reading checks; more rigorous curriculum and exams; technical academies; performance transparency; pupil premium for disadvantaged children; expand academies/free schools; protect and improve special education.

Crime, policing and borders
- Tougher knife crime sentencing; overhaul licensing to curb alcohol‑related disorder; early‑intervention sanctions for antisocial behaviour.
- Cut police paperwork; restore local accountability via directly elected oversight; publish street‑level crime data; create a Border Police Force; payment‑by‑results rehabilitation; expand abstinence‑based drug treatment.

Civil liberties and political reform
- Scrap ID cards and large central databases; rebalance DNA retention; reform libel law; scale back vetting systems.
- Recall for MPs; tighter expenses/lobbying rules; reduce the size and cost of central government and quangos; open data on spending, contracts, salaries; citizen petitions with parliamentary debates; fairer constituency sizes.
- Localism: neighbourhood‑led planning; abolish regional spatial strategies; community rights to run/buy local assets; local referendums; more elected city mayors.

Energy, environment and rural
- 80% emissions cut by 2050; smart grid/meters; nuclear (no subsidy), CCS projects, offshore grid, marine energy; Green Investment Bank; carbon price floor; Green Deal for home efficiency.
- Protect habitats and biodiversity; reform fisheries and agriculture policies; sustainable procurement; supermarket ombudsman; targeted badger control for bovine TB; national tree‑planting; move toward zero‑waste.

Defense, foreign policy and development
- National Security Council; strategic defence review; improve procurement; maintain nuclear deterrent; enhance support for service personnel and families.
- Active global engagement; safeguard energy security; EU “referendum lock” on future power transfers; sovereignty legislation; seek return of select powers.
- Aid at 0.7% of national income by 2013 with transparency, results focus, malaria funding, and emphasis on the poorest and on trade‑led growth.
